## Approach

For this assignment, I'm using the penguin_predictions.csv dataset from the
course GitHub, which contains a model's predicted probability of "female"
alongside the actual sex label. My plan is to first check the null error
rate and class balance, since that sets the baseline any threshold needs to
beat. Then I'll recompute the predicted class myself from .pred_female at
three thresholds (0.2, 0.5, 0.8) instead of relying on the given
.pred_class column, build a confusion matrix at each one, and derive
accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 from those counts.

The main challenge I anticipate isn't technical, since the dataset is
small and clean, but conceptual: understanding why accuracy alone doesn't
tell the full story, and being able to explain in plain terms why a lower
threshold trades precision for recall (and vice versa) rather than just
reporting the numbers without interpretation.
